messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing bursty exporter restarts on a subset of GPU nodes which is causing scrape storms and a big Prometheus ingestion spike. Last hour: ~12 nodes, ~200 restarts each.

ajay: Yikes. I pulled a couple logs, looks like node-exporter getting killed (exit 137) then systemd immediately restarts it. Also seeing dcgm-exporter report `kv cache invalidation` then hang. Snippet: 

```
Mar 12 02:11:03 gpu-node-42 systemd[1]: node-exporter.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=137/n/a
Mar 12 02:11:03 gpu-node-42 systemd[1]: Stopping Node Exporter...
Mar 12 02:11:03 gpu-node-42 systemd[1]: Started Node Exporter.
Mar 12 02:21:15 gpu-node-42 dcgm-exporter[1234]: WARN kv cache invalidation: seq=9283
Mar 12 02:21:16 gpu-node-42 dcgm-exporter[1234]: ERROR stuck waiting on kernel response
```

ajay: Also saw kubelet eviction logs on two nodes around the same window, memory pressure spikes.

leo: This matches a pattern we saw last quarter when a driver hotpatch changed kernel memory accounting and DCGM started allocating more pinned memory. But the restart loop shouldn't amplify Prometheus cardinality like this. Two quick suggestions: soften restart aggression and add staleness-based restarts instead of immediate pid restarts.

kai: Agreed. Proposal: deploy an `exporter-watchdog` sidecar (or systemd service) that monitors the exporter metrics endpoint and only restarts exporter if the `/metrics` endpoint is stale for >10m AND restart_count > 3 within 30m. That avoids 1-off crashes blowing up scrape counts. Also adjust Prom scrape manager: increase scrape_timeout slightly and set `honor_timestamps`?

maria: I like the watchdog idea. Do we have code for that?

ajay: We actually have a small script in infra/tools: `exporter-watchdog` (bash + small Go helper) that did something similar for node-exporter last year but wasn't enabled on gpu pools. I can flip a canary. Basic behavior: poll `/metrics` every 30s, if content timestamp delta > 600s -> attempt graceful restart, limit restarts with exponential backoff.

kai: For k8s DaemonSet, prefer livenessProbe/readinessProbe tuning over immediate restarts. Example k8s snippet we should use for canary: 

```
livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /-/healthy
    port: 9100
  initialDelaySeconds: 60
  periodSeconds: 30
  failureThreshold: 6
readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /-/ready
    port: 9100
  initialDelaySeconds: 15
  periodSeconds: 15
  failureThreshold: 4
```

kai: Also add `restartPolicy: Always` but with `maxRestartsPerMinute` baked into the sidecar logic (since k8s lacks a pluggable backoff policy per container).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout: infra/exporter-watchdog v1.2 -> 5 nodes in pool `us-west2-gpu-pool`. Watch for prom_scrape_errors_high and exporter_restart_rate alerts.

sre-bot: ALERT firing: prom_scrape_errors_high (cluster=gpu-pool) — 1200 errors/min, 7m. Alert tags: severity=high, team=eng-infra.

maria: OK action plan: 1) ajay start canary on 5 nodes (us-west2) and monitor ingestion rate + cardinality; 2) kai update DaemonSet probes and add readiness gating; 3) leo run a quick memory driver sanity check on the patched nodes; 4) if canary looks good (10m stable) roll to remaining GPU pools.

ajay: Starting canary now. I'll post updates every 5m.

(5m later)

ajay: Canary update: exporter restarts on the 5 canary nodes dropped from ~30/min to 1-2 per hour after watchdog enabled. Prom ingestion rate down ~65%. Still seeing dcgm warning on 2 nodes; flagged for leo.

leo: I'll take those two nodes off rotation and run `nvidia-smi -q` + `dmesg` to confirm kernel OOMs. If driver is culprit we should schedule a maintenance window for driver rollback.

kai: Next follow-ups: add a Prom recording rule `exporter_restart_rate:sum_over_time` and a dashboard panel for 'Exporters: restart smoothing' to track restarts per node over 1h/6h windows. That will make future rollouts faster.

maria: Thanks all — this is a good small-step fix. Long-term follow-ups: (A) integrate watchdog into the GPU image, (B) add automatic cordon + notify if restart_rate > threshold for 30m, (C) evaluate Prometheus retention/cost impact from these flaps (we dumped ~20GB/day of high-card metrics during the spike).

ajay: FYI the canary rollout command I used: 
```
kubectl -n infra patch daemonset gpu-exporters -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"exporter-watchdog","image":"ghcr.io/redwood/exporter-watchdog:v1.2","imagePullPolicy":"IfNotPresent"}]}}}}'
```

maria: Closing loop: if no regression in 30m we'll roll to prod. I'll open a short postmortem doc with timeline and cost delta. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: RESOLVE prom_scrape_errors_high — alert cleared after canary stabilization (total errors/min down to 120).
